prompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: native transparent tactical-game combat sprite, C01-UNIT-CANNON-WAGON, IDLE pose, first master of a four-pose animation.
Primary request: Remake the exact single covered cannon wagon and its ONE original crew member from reference 1 in the approved chunky matte cel style of references 2 and 3. Reference 1 is the sole subject/topology/palette authority. Reference 2 gives bold simple cart construction and material planes only; never borrow its crossbow, operator, extra wheels or helmet. Reference 3 gives chunky human proportions and very bold outlines only; do not borrow its costume or weapons.
Subject identity: One compact warm-brown timber wagon viewed from slightly above in three-quarter side view, facing RIGHT. Preserve the big tan canvas arched cover over its rear upper body, with a dark opening facing right behind the gun; simple broad canvas folds. Preserve the short warm BRASS cannon projecting RIGHT from the front, with a large open dark muzzle, broad raised brass barrel rings and two small round trunnion mounts on the timber chassis. Preserve gray iron corner brackets on the thick wooden chassis and low front bumper. Preserve the open side tray of dark round cannonballs next to the canvas hood. Preserve the hanging orange-brown rectangular front-side panel with its simple ochre angular rune motif; no readable letters. Exactly the two visible source wheel silhouettes: one LARGE near-side wooden spoked wheel below the tray, and the partially occluded SMALLER front wheel below the cannon/bumper. Do not expose additional wheels, stretch the chassis or change axle topology.
Original crew: Exactly ONE compact short adult at the rear-left of the cart, black hair and red tied headband, clean-shaven focused face, charcoal neck scarf, gray short-sleeved tunic with brown leather vest/straps, brown bracers and pouches, dark trousers, sturdy brown boots. One hand rests on the cart's rear side grip; the other carries the same small gray iron spanner low diagonally by the knees. The crew is naturally shorter than the wagon cover, around 70 percent of the complete wagon height. Preserve this original crew identity, placement and tools. No helmet, shield, sword, extra operator, animal or horse.
Idle pose: Stationary transport stance, boots grounded in a small comfortable stagger, wheels grounded, cannon level and unfired. Canvas and orange rune panel hang at rest. No smoke, flash, sparks or glow in idle.
Style/medium: Strong chunky silhouettes, very bold charcoal contour and broad simplified material planes, matte finish, only two or three cel-shaded tones per material. Large readable spokes, chunky cannon rings and generous clear open gaps. No fine woodgrain, scratches, stitching grids, canvas weave, small rivet fields, tiny faceted noise, photorealism, painterly grain, gloss or airbrush shading.
Composition/framing: One complete assembly only, centered on a landscape 1536 by 1024 transparent canvas. Keep original relative crew/cart size, orientation and silhouette. Fill about 82 percent of width, allow generous transparent margins around every extremity including the muzzle, both boots, wheels and canopy. Leave clear right-side space for later firing pose without changing scale. Stable slightly elevated three-quarter camera. No crop or panel sheet.
Background: Genuine transparent alpha outside the assembly and through open wheel spokes and limb gaps. No scenery, floor, ground disk, cast-shadow puddle, exterior halo, opaque backdrop, checkerboard paint, labels, captions or watermark. The background must be truly transparent.
